tagline: One spec.md per task, an append-only ledger, and a handoff another agent can pick up.
bestFor: Work that outlives one session and may move between agents, machines, or accounts
keyFeatures: One `spec.md` per unit of work with Problem, Scope, numbered acceptance criteria (`AC-01`), Approach, and Tasks; each task names its AC, files, and a test command
Append-only `ledger.jsonl` of task claims, completions, blocks, notes, handoffs, and pickups; lines are never edited, and state is derived by folding the log
`specweave task done` requires evidence: `--run "<cmd>"` stores the exit code and a log and refuses a failing command, while `--evidence` accepts free text

`specweave verify` runs configured test commands, or the project's detected `test`, `lint`, and `build` scripts (or `cargo test`, `pytest`, `go test`), and `specweave complete` reads its report as the closure gate

`specweave handoff` releases the agent's claims, writes a handoff note, pushes the branch, and pushes a snapshot of uncommitted work to a `specweave-handoff` ref; `specweave pickup` in another tool or account applies it and prints the next task with its ACs
`specweave auto-handoff on` reads plan usage from the Claude Code status line and Codex session logs; the default suggests a handoff at 95% of a window, and `--mode enforce` stops and hands off
One short `AGENTS.md` shared by Codex, Grok Build, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode, with `CLAUDE.md` importing it (project's claim for the agent list, not tested here)
A hook blocks edits made without an increment unless `specweave small-fix "<why>"` is run, and each exemption is logged; `specweave dashboard` serves a local web dashboard
limitations: One author wrote about 95% of 3,856 commits; 173 stars and 20 forks on 2026-11-20, repository created 2025-10-25

The CLI sits under a commercial layer: SpecWithCode, a desktop app with a hosted relay, a $20/month Pro tier on a waitlist, team contracts, and a paid pilot; the pricing page says the CLI and app stay free (project's claim, not tested here)
Handoff cannot carry another tool's session transcript; continuity depends on files kept in git, and tracker sync (GitHub, Jira, Azure DevOps) runs only on demand
No worktree creation, no MCP server in the CLI, and no first-party IDE extension found; parallel lanes share one checkout and are guided by a skill (our inference from the source)
Evidence is weaker than the wording suggests: `--evidence` takes free text and a ticked AC checkbox counts as met (our inference from the source)

The project's docs disagree on defaults: the README and pricing page say auto-handoff at 90%, while the code and guide say 95% in suggest mode; the "about 760 tokens" AGENTS.md figure describes the 3.0 template
Requested by the maintainer (conflict disclosed in issue #57); scores are this repo's, assessed from the source, the 3.2.2 package, and docs on 2026-11-20, not from hands-on use
